title: MAILED! The Girl & The Champion Who Posted Themselves
sources: Smithsonian National Postal Museum, 'Very Special Deliveries': May Pierstorff was mailed February 19, 1914, Grangeville to Lewiston Idaho (73 miles), 53 cents in stamps on her coat, just short of the 50 lb parcel limit

Wikipedia 'Charlotte May Pierstorff' (48.5 lb; rode the mail car with Leonard Mochel, her mother's cousin, a railway postal clerk; parcel post began January 1, 1913; regulations later that year banned mailing people; day-old poultry stayed mailable)
USPS postal regulations: day-old poultry (baby chicks) is still mailable today

Wikipedia 'Reg Spiers': born Adelaide 14 December 1941 (so age 22 in 1964); over two metres tall; third at the 1960/61 Australian championships, second 1961/62; fifth at the 1962 Commonwealth Games in Perth with a best javelin throw of 69.70 m; failed to make the 1964 Olympic team; near-dehydration in Mumbai

BBC News Magazine 31700049, 'The man who posted himself to Australia' (interviews with Reg Spiers and John McSorley): 1964, crate 5x3x2.5 ft, sent COD as 'a load of paint' to a fictitious shoe company, 24-h fog delay, got out between London and Paris, pee can on the crate, French handlers blamed the English, Bombay 4 hours upside down in the sun, Perth landing, 63 hours / three days, escaped the bond shed with tools, free beer (he doesn't drink), suit, out the window, hitchhike; McSorley alerted the press via Daily Telegraph sports correspondent James Coote; media storm for weeks; airline never charged; telegram 'a gallant effort by a real Aussie - and here's five quid'; made it home in time for the birthday; wife didn't believe him at first
The New York Times, Nov 7, 1964, 'Australian, Penniless in London, Is Flown Home in Crate, C.O.D.'
